question: How do aggregation and incorrect video grouping change the measured effect of inference L2 across the three frozen backbones?
interpretation: Compare matched L2-minus-Raw effects, and their grouping interaction, without treating a larger gain as a higher absolute AUC.
scope: Frozen formal D models and original strict five-seed summaries only; no retraining, inference, selection, or new confidence interval.

a.comparison: L2 AUC minus Raw AUC under correct natural-video grouping
a.purpose: Estimate the inference intervention before changing the video definition.

b.comparison: (L2 minus Raw) under collision grouping minus (L2 minus Raw) under correct grouping
b.purpose: Measure how the evaluation rule changes the inferred benefit; positive interaction alone is not a sign reversal.

source_data: All eight absolute AUC cells and all five seeds per selected backbone and TEST domain; paired panel values and their sample-SD summaries.
replication: Five matched training seeds: 7, 42, 123, 2026, 3407. CAL subsets, video pairs, and bootstrap draws do not increase this n.
uncertainty: Mean and sample SD (ddof=1) of within-seed differences; all individual training seeds shown. No new target TEST CI.
exclusions: No selected backbone, seed, grouping, aggregation, or representation omitted from absolute-AUC Source Data. Panels display the two pre-specified contrasts; original collision deltas remain available in the bound strict summary.
acceptance: Complete strict summary plus source-analysis identity, committed artifact hashes, exact matched cells, and effect reconstruction. Real rendering waits for those gates.
qa: Render-time strict panel alignment, source preflight, PDF glyph floor, collision audit, all-panel visual inspection. Minimum intended text size 7pt; absolute glyph floor 5pt.
decision: Routine extension of the approved final-figure deliverable using the existing Python workflow; scientific estimates and frozen experimental choices are unchanged.
